description: The plot illustrates how two metrics—perplexity and GPU memory ratio—vary as a function of the recent sequence ratio. The x-axis is labeled “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” on a linear scale, spanning roughly 10% to 100% with labeled ticks at 20% intervals (20, 40, 60, 80, 100). The left y-axis is labeled “Perplexity” on a linear scale from about 4.2 to 4.7 with ticks every 0.1, and the right y-axis is labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)” on a linear scale from about 40% to 100% with ticks every 10%. One orange solid line with circular markers labeled “Perplexity” starts near 4.59 at 10%, decreases to about 4.45 at 20% and ~4.39 at 30%, reaches a low around 4.30 at 40%, then rises to ~4.33 at 50% and ~4.34 at 60%, dips slightly to ~4.29 at 70%, increases to ~4.33 at 80%, rises to ~4.39 at 90%, and ends near ~4.38 at 100%; a red dashed horizontal reference line labeled “Full Cache PPL” sits at approximately 4.38 across all x-values. A blue solid line with circular markers labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio” begins around 40% at 10% recent sequence ratio, increases gradually through roughly 41% (20%), 42% (30%), 43% (40%), 44% (50%), 45% (60%), and ~47% (70%), rises to about 55% at 80%, then jumps sharply to about 98% at 90% and ends near 99–100% at 100%; a blue dashed horizontal reference line labeled “Full Cache GPU Mem.” lies near 100% across the plot.
